blocks.x: Personalization rebuilt on evaluated retrieval — watch time per session up 11% and catalog long-tail exposure up 2.6x
a streaming platform whose recommendation row was famous and whose long tail was not. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline month measured the fame gap: 74% of viewing from the top 5% of catalog, 19% of sessions ending without a play, and every A/B proposal from editorial argued on taste because no evaluation baseline existed.
Popularity dominated ranking because engagement signals were the only objective. New titles and niche catalogs never accumulated the signals that would surface them.

We rebuilt personalization as evaluated retrieval: multi-objective ranking balancing engagement, satisfaction signals and catalog exposure, exploration budget managed explicitly so long-tail titles earn impressions, offline evaluation on labeled sessions gating every model change, and editorial tooling showing predicted impact per row so taste arguments became experiments. The tail found its audience.
